body.en: Roots can be written as radicals or as fractional exponents; both obey the laws of exponents.
\( \sqrt{ab}=\sqrt{a}\,\sqrt{b} \), \( a^{1/n}=\sqrt[n]{a} \), and \( a^{m/n}=\sqrt[n]{a^{m}} \). Rationalise a denominator by multiplying by the conjugate.

Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Radicals & Exponents)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

Rationalize the denominator: \( \dfrac{6}{3 - \sqrt{3}} \).

Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \( 3 + \sqrt{3} \):

\[ \frac{6(3 + \sqrt{3})}{(3 - \sqrt{3})(3 + \sqrt{3})} = \frac{18 + 6\sqrt{3}}{3^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2} = \frac{18 + 6\sqrt{3}}{9 - 3} = \frac{18 + 6\sqrt{3}}{6} = 3 + \sqrt{3}. \]

label.en: Common Pitfall — Splitting Radicals Over Addition & Extraneous Roots

body.en: Two crucial rules for radicals: 1. Never split over addition: \( \sqrt{a^2 + b^2} \neq a + b \) (for example, \( \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5 \), NOT \( 3 + 4 = 7 \)). You can only split radicals over multiplication and division. 2. Extraneous solutions: Squaring both sides of an equation can introduce false roots. You MUST substitute candidate solutions back into the original un-squared equation.

label.en: Worked Example C — Radicals & Exponents (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): The positive variables \( A \) and \( B \) are inversely proportional such that \( B = 160 \) when \( A = 6 \). Compute the value of \( B(n) \) when \( A = 8 \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Since \( AB = 960 \), when \( A = 8 \) we have \( B = 120 \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Radicals & Exponents (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): A scatterplot has least-squares regression line \( \hat{A}(n) = 18n + 5 \). Compute the predicted value \( \hat{A}(10) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Substituting \( n = 10 \) gives \( 18(10) + 5 = 185 \).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Radicals & Exponents)

rows.en: Confuses the product law \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\) with a non-existent sum rule.
Only factor products, quotients, and powers inside logarithms: \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\).
Keeping both roots of \(\sqrt{2x+5} = x - 2\) without checking \(x - 2 \ge 0\)
Squaring both sides loses the sign of \(x - {r}\), introducing roots where \(\sqrt{\cdot} = -\text{number}\).
Enforce the range condition \(x \ge 2\) before or after squaring.
Restricting domain of \(f(x) = (x-3)^2 + 1\) to \(x \ge 0\) for invertibility
The vertex is at \(x = 3\), so \(f(2) = f(4) = 2\) fails the horizontal line test on \(x \ge 0\).
Restrict the domain at the vertex axis of symmetry: \(x \ge 3\) (or \(x \le 3\)).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Radicals & Exponents

body.en: Fast Exam Check (Honors Algebra 1 & Foundations): To verify an inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) in 5 seconds, pick a simple input \(x_0\), compute \(y_0 = f(x_0)\), and check that \(f^{-1}(y_0) = x_0\). Also verify that the graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) reflects \(y = f(x)\) across \(y = x\).

question.en: Solve the equation \( \sqrt{2x + 7} = x + 2 \) for all real values of \( x \).

solution.en:
Square both sides of the equation:

\[ (\sqrt{2x + 7})^2 = (x + 2)^2 \implies 2x + 7 = x^2 + 4x + 4. \]

Rearrange into standard quadratic form:

\[ x^2 + 2x - 3 = 0 \implies (x + 3)(x - 1) = 0 \implies x = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -3. \]

Now check both candidate roots in the original equation:

  • For \( x = 1 \): LHS = \( \sqrt{2(1) + 7} = \sqrt{9} = 3 \); RHS = \( 1 + 2 = 3 \). (Valid ✓)
  • For \( x = -3 \): LHS = \( \sqrt{2(-3) + 7} = \sqrt{1} = 1 \); RHS = \( -3 + 2 = -1 \). Since \( 1 \neq -1 \), \( x = -3 \) is extraneous.

The only real solution is \( x = 1 \).
